title: An optimised method for the production of MERS-CoV spike expressing viral pseudotypes
author: Grehan, Ferrara, et al.

steps.title: Seed 293T/17 cells
steps.instruction: Subculture 293T/17 cells into 100 mm Petri dishes at a density that will give 70–90 % confluence at transfection time (any dish size acceptable if supernatant yield is equivalent).

steps.title: Pre‑warm media
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm DMEM containing 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (P/S) and Opti‑MEM® to 37 °C in a water bath or equivalent.

steps.title: Label microcentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Label two sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes as “tube 1” and “tube 2” for each transfection.

steps.title: Prepare DNA mixture
steps.instruction: In tube 1 add 0.9 µg pCAGGS‑MERS‑CoV spike plasmid, 1.0 µg p8.91‑lentiviral vector plasmid, and 1.5 µg pCSFLW plasmid (envelope:core:vector ratio 0.9:1:1.5), then add 200 µl Opti‑MEM® and mix gently.

steps.title: Prepare PEI mixture
steps.instruction: In tube 2 add 200 µl Opti‑MEM® and 35 µl of 1 mg ml⁻¹ polyethylenimine (PEI), mix gently.

steps.title: Combine DNA and PEI
steps.instruction: Flick both tubes gently and incubate at room temperature (RT) for 5 min; then add the entire contents of tube 2 to tube 1, flick to mix, and incubate at RT for an additional 20 min, flicking every 3–4 min.

steps.title: Replace cell culture medium
steps.instruction: While the transfection mix incubates, aspirate the existing medium from the 293T/17 cells and add 7 ml fresh DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S slowly to one side of each 100 mm dish to avoid detaching cells.

steps.title: Add transfection mixture
steps.instruction: After the 20 min incubation, add the DNA/Opti‑MEM/PEI mixture dropwise over the entire surface of the plate, then swirl the plate gently to ensure even distribution.

steps.title: First incubation (overnight)
steps.instruction: Incubate the transfected plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 12–16 h (overnight).

steps.title: Replace medium post‑overnight
steps.instruction: After the overnight incubation, remove the medium and add 7 ml fresh DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S slowly to one side of each dish.

steps.title: Second incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for an additional 32–36 h.

steps.title: Harvest pseudotype supernatant
steps.instruction: At 44–52 h post‑transfection, collect supernatant using a 10 ml sterile syringe, filter through a syringe‑driven Millex HA 0.45 µm filter into sterile Falcon tubes, and store aliquots at –80 °C (or at 4 °C for up to one week if used immediately).

steps.title: Optional second harvest
steps.instruction: To obtain a second harvest, add fresh DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S to the cells 18–24 h after the first collection, taking extreme care not to disturb the monolayer; then repeat the harvest procedure.

steps.title: Generate Δ‑env control
steps.instruction: Follow steps 1‑12 but omit the pCAGGS‑MERS‑CoV spike plasmid; the resulting particles lack the viral surface glycoprotein (Δ‑env control).

steps.title: Add media to cell‑only wells
steps.instruction: In a white 96‑well plate add 50 µl DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S to every well of column 12 (cell‑only control).

steps.title: Add media to virus columns
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S to wells in rows B–H of the columns designated for pseudotyped virus or Δ‑env control.

steps.title: Add virus and Δ‑env controls
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl MERS‑CoV pseudotype supernatant to each well of row A (excluding control columns) and add 100 µl Δ‑env supernatant to column 11.

steps.title: Perform 1:2 serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Remove 50 µl from each virus‑containing well in row A, transfer to the next well down, mix by pipetting up and down eight times, repeat down the column, and discard the final 50 µl from the last well of each column.

steps.title: Prepare Huh‑7 target cells
steps.instruction: Prepare a plate of susceptible Huh‑7 target cells (subcultured 1:4 48 h prior) as follows.

substeps.instruction: Wash the plate with 2 ml trypsin and discard the trypsin.
Add 2 ml trypsin to the plate to detach cells.
Add DMEM/10 % FBS/1 % P/S to quench trypsin activity.
Count cells and dispense 1 × 10⁴ cells in 50 µl into each well of the assay plate.

steps.title: Centrifuge plate (optional)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 1 min at 500 rpm if droplets adhere to the sides of the wells.

steps.title: Incubate infection
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 48 h.

steps.title: Measure luciferase activity
steps.instruction: Read luminescence using the Bright Glo™ luciferase assay system (or equivalent) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

description: Fig. 2 displays data recorded from multiple transfections indicating consistency of results. Results are measured in Relative Luminescence Units (RLUs) as measured using a GloMax® 96 Microplate Luminometer and the Bright Glo™ luciferase assay system. The pseudotype particles generated in the absence of viral envelope (Delta) show increased luciferase activity compared to cell only in part due to transformation method used to discern RLU per ml. The presence of some carry-over luciferase within viral particles is also likely to generate an increase in RLU values recorded (Table 1). Fig. 3 shows percentage neutralisation of the MERS-CoV pseudotype with commercially produced anti-MERS spike antibody. Figure clearly indicates that as the dilution factor increases, so the percentage neutralisation decreases, 100% neutralisation indicates that RLU values at this concentration are equivalent to a delta envelope control. The protocol outlined here provides a rapid and consistent method for the generation of high-titre viral pseudotype particles expressing the MERS-CoV spike protein suitable for further downstream applications [2], [4], [5], [7]. Efficient knock-down of pseudotype virus entry using a polyclonal antibody directed against the spike glycoprotein (Fig. 3) demonstrates potential utility for vaccine immunogenicity and Mab/antiviral screening [3]. The use of readily available reagents should facilitate increased reproducibility [1], [6], [9], [10], [11], [12].
